content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm working on a program where I need to generate a pulse output each time an input or memory bit changes state, either from low to high or high to low. Any change in the input should result in a pulse. I would appreciate any assistance.
You can refer to the attached example image. Utilizing the AND (Edge) and NAND (Edge) logic blocks is helpful for this. The up/down counter should just count the pulses produced.
Hi, I noticed the counter shows the output state, but not the pulse itself. Could you please explain your example in more detail? Also, what function does the open collector block serve?

I did not state that the up/down counter is responsible for generating the pulses; it should only count them. The actual pulses are created by the AND (Edge) and NAND (Edge) blocks, which are combined using an OR block. The OR block's output goes high for one cycle each time the input changes state. The open collector is used to close the output from the counter.
Hello, Could you provide a timing diagram to illustrate what you are requesting? I believe I understand your requirement, and this visual might clarify things. [IMAGE]

Hi everyone, thank you for your assistance. I've tried applying your suggestions, but I'm having difficulty picturing the solution. I've included an image to illustrate my situation more clearly. Hoping for further guidance. Appreciate your commitment.
Take another look at the logic provided by @ixo65. The segment to the left of the counter demonstrates how to generate the required pulses. The counter is included to make the effect visible.
That's correct, thank you all for your support. I had overlooked your advice, but my problem is now resolved.
